items.text: I wish AB beauty trend / beauty standard in general is less obsessed with snow white fair skin. AB skincare products can be great, but I've also grown up with and seen so many skincare products focused on whitening (not brightening) on the shelves, and make up colour palettes that flatter fair skin but not even the slightly tan skin. Even Hada Labo ads would boasts whitening. I also know many people don't even wear foundation that matches their skin tone, they just buy the foundation shade fairer than they actually are.

I love your drawing! So cute.

Hmm, you could consider removing micellar water or oil. It seems like you basically have triple cleansing, I would think it’s usually a bit too much. But maybe it works for you. For me I recently switched from micellar water (mine was Garnier micellar water) to oil double cleansing, since oil does better and more anyway.

Hi guys, I just started using Cosrx Balancium Comfort Ceramide Cream (it’s been great so far) and Laneige Water Sleeping Mask. And I’m not too sure which one should go on my face first. The cream is quite thick but the water sleeping mask sounds like it should be the last step but the texture is lighter. Any idea? Or how would you go about this?
I’d recommend Vitamin C in the morning too. It protects against pollution and free radicals if I’m not mistaken. Just be sure to use a sunscreen too.
That’s a good idea. Thank you!
I apply it straight on my lips. Sometimes I Apple after lip balm though cause my lips can be dry.

Wow that’s some really stubborn eye make up! Yea you can use micellar after oil cleansing if needed. Maybe look for a better oil cleanser that could remove your mascara, or even a make up remover specifically for your eyes so you don’t over cleanse your face.

I just started using Cosrx Balancium Comfort Cream (mainly for its ceramide content) for a few days and I love it so far! I don’t know if my skin was irritated or breaking out or moisture barrier was damaged, whatever it was this helped the most to fix that issue. The formula is thicker than I’m used to though. 

I just bought Skin1004 Centella Ampoule and I can’t wait to try it.
I second this! It's called L'Oreal Double Extend.
I use Maybelline Baby Lips but it's only SPF 15. It's tinted so you can use it alone. I'm thinking of maybe getting Sebamed Lip Defense SPF 30 next time.

It's probably not good but I'd still at least use my tinted sunscreen and concealer to cover it up a little. I have paler skin and a pimple looks so red and obvious on my skin, it feels like it's constantly asking for everyone to look at it. I can't stand it. But if it's a less obvious spot or I can get away with using Cosrx pimple patch without looking weird I'd do that. I tried applying make up over the pimple patch and it did not look good at all.
I've heard that TO's niacinamide pills. Maybe you could switch it to PM, I've heard that it works well with retinols.

I wish applying matte liquid lipsticks can be easier. The colours are so bold that any tiny mistakes would be so obvious. I have to make sure the line is clean and nice, top and bottom lips are relatively even, and for me, careful to not over-line my lips. Even before applying, I have to exfoliate my dry lips, moisturise them, then put on lip liner first. After applying I'd try to clean up any mistakes with make up remover or concealer. The process can be so tedious but I absolutely loveee my make up looks with matte liquid lipsticks, and they're so long lasting and don't budge at all that it makes it worth it.

I’ve been so pissed with Colourpop and their CS service and USPS. I ordered from them end of February, and I live in Asia so I’ve been very patiently waiting for the package to arrive. They say it takes 10-21 business days so okay. The USPS tracking wasn’t moving though so I emailed them to check and they reassured me that it’s fine, package is in transit and probably just missing a scan.

And guess what I found out on the 21st business day? No package. Check the USPS tracker, and it finally has an update... that it finally left LA and is currently in transit to me.

I got so angry! Their tracker wasn’t updated for a whole month, and I believed them when they said it’s just missing a scan. Turns out the package never left LA to begin with! It was in LA or USPS warehouse, unmoved for a whole month! Or it just took one whole month to move from one part to LA to another part of LA. The package should be arriving by now, not finally on its way to me now a month later. And Colourpop’s customer service is absolutely useless, even after telling them of this disaster, they just tell me “it’s on the way”. Nothing useful, no attempts to fix this or make this better, not even an apology. Just a nonchalant robotic reply. And now instead of the 10-21 business days they kept reassuring me with, I’m possibly waiting for 42 business days, if the package ever arrives. I’ve shopped with them before and this is hands down, by far, my worst online shopping experience. So disappointed with Colourpop / Fourth Ray.

I agree with others. I don't think these ingredients are inherently bad, but they just may not work for more people, and for these people's sake, it's good to have a safe option. I think fragrance, essential oils and alcohol are ultimately fine as long as your skin can tolerate them. I personally prefer lighter weight gel moisturisers and if I'm not mistaken they always contain alcohol. Even for fragrance, it might not do anything good for your skin, but I know many people appreciate a skincare product that smells great because it feels luxurious and adds to the experience, especially if they're unwinding or treating themselves. Or fragrance could be added to cover a product's less-than-ideal smell. I'm not sure if Cosrx BHA Power Liquid is fragrance-free, but man that product did not smell good and took me a while to get used to it.

It's actually fairly easy to get skincare products in Thailand and Malaysia, maybe you can drop by the mall for Sephora or local drugstores (Malaysia has Watson's and Guardian) when you're visiting the city or in the airport if you need anything. We have access to quite a lot of brands and it's easy to shop online here too.

Maybe that’s why Colourpop is always releasing shiny new products, to distract from their inconsistent shipping. I was surprised because my previous experiences with them were normal, but one google search shows that many have had to deal with various shipping issues.
Whattt that is horrible! Their CS just sounds worse every time. I hope I don’t have to deal with that. If I don’t get my package I’m going to try getting my money back via PayPal.

items.title: Distorted peripheral vision after a month with new glasses
items.text:
Distorted peripheral vision after a month with new glasses
Hi everyone! I've been wearing my new glasses for short-sightedness for almost a month now and it was quite a drastic change, and I still experience a bit of peripheral distortion and I'm not too sure that it's normal. The context is, I've had my previous (smaller, rectangle) glasses for maybe 8-9 years (I'm 26) and had changed to a new bigger, square-ish wayfarer glasses. It's a large increase in power (3.75 to 5 and 4.75), increase in the glasses size, and I was wearing the old one for so long so it's a long adjustment period. I also got the lenses to be thinner. But it's been a month and my peripheral distortion did not go away, so I went back and switched to a slighter smaller frame and things have improved. I even drove with it and it seemed fine. I also wear contact lenses when I go out and didn't experience such problem even after updating my prescription.

&#x200B;

What I'm not so sure is, is it normal if I still experience a tinyy bit of peripheral distortion? Specifically, when I take the stairs, I keep my head straight forward but my eyes look down, there's a tiny bit of distortion, stairs look slightlyyy bent (but not as bad as the previous frame). I tested the same by holding a round object and looking down with my head straight, and this time the round shape doesn't look oval (I think) unlike the previous bigger frame. Is this part normal? Should I go get something changed again?

&#x200B;

***New Prescription***

* *Prescription: 5.00 (R), 4.75 (L)*
* *Lens Index: 1.67*
* *Frame Material: Plastic matte*
* *Axis: 25 (R) 165 (L)*

***Old Prescription:****(If Applicable)*

* *Prescription: 3.75 for both*
* *Axis: 20 (R) 155 (L)*

&#x200B;

If anyone knows if this is normal and I can just keep this new frame, or go get it changed again, that'd be great! Thank you.

If I'm not mistaken, you don't need a high concentration of niacinamide for it to be effective and 4-5% should be just fine. TO's 10% niacinamide can actually be too strong and irritating for some people.
Might not be the site you were looking for but [reissue.co](https://reissue.co) does the same thing, but they don't have too many products on the site.
Thank you! Seems like the store just didn't have or consider these things. How likely is it that I get used to it eventually if I stick with this?

Are you introducing the new products all at the same time? Without knowing much, your skin could be irritated from suddenly being introduced to so many products, or maybe one of them is breaking you out. If so, try stopping all and reintroducing one by one and patch test first. Could also be the stress from work (if it’s stressful) or change in lifestyle or lack of sleep.
Anyone knows any dupe for Kiehl’s Ultra Facial Cream? I loved the sample I got but I can’t justify the price. Any cheaper dupes? Thanks!
Remove mine please!

Try looking for moisturizers in gel or light cream form. I use Hada Labo Hydrating Water Gel.I tested Hada Labo Hydrating Light Cream on my hand the other day and it felt very light too. I do use the 7-skin method and layer some hydrating toners before moisturizer. I live in similar climate and another non-AB moisturizer I like is Kiehl's Ultra Facial Cream, did not feel heavy at all.
Maybe you could use it on the rest of your body as a body lotion!

I didn’t like Simple’s make up remover wipes, it was so dry and wasn’t great at removing make up. I prefer Biore but now I’ve just stopped using make up wipes.

I had a bad experience with Garnier Light Brightening Eye Roll-on. Never figured out why though, could just be my skin does not agree with an ingredient. It was otherwise fun to use.

Unpopular opinion but I don’t think I like the Nivea Creme in blue tin. I personally think it’s not very spreadable and thus hard to use. It’s otherwise fine.

I alwaysss wear a sunscreen (Biore aqua rich watery essence) underneath make up, and I use Biore tinted sunscreen on lazier days where I'm only going out for a short while and not under the sun much. They're both SPF50++++ and I don't find them greasy. I don't reapply sunscreen though because I don't want to disturb my makeup.

I might try spray-on sunscreens or buy an empty cushion case and fill it with my sunscreen. The only thing is I feel both methods still would disturb my make up a little bit. Even spray ons are supposed to be sprayed on palm then pat on face.
